content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple OOMs detected on gpu-prod-23 cluster (CUDA errors + container crashes). Rate spike at 11:20 UTC. Affected service: serving-runtime. Link: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/1749990000

mike: oncall here. assigning to myself for triage. which nodes exactly?

infra-bot: node events: prod-23-04 restarted container serving-runtime x3 in 12m, reason: OOM_KILL (kernel report: CONTEXT_INFO: 'CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH failed'), network OK, disk <70%

ashley: I see a slow mem creep on KV cache for high-concurrency sessions — per-gpu memory used by kv-cache increasing without releasing. Not sudden alloc spike, more fragmentation + slow leak. Sample logs show repeated page-scan failures around cache compaction.

ashley: relevant snippet:
```
[11:15:02] kv_cache: page_scan: freed=0, scanned=128, contiguous=4
[11:17:09] gpu_mem: allocated=1234MB, resident=1176MB, fragmentation=0.42
[11:19:58] runtime: kernel launch error: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED (code=9)
[11:20:01] container: oom_kill, pid=4821, cmd=serving-runtime
```

carlos: copying dmesg and nvidia-smi from prod-23-04:
```
$ ssh prod-23-04 sudo dmesg | tail -n 20
[53789.112345] Out of memory: Kill process 4821 (serving-runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
[53789.112789] Killed process 4821 (serving-runtime) total-vm:12345678kB, anon-rss:11987600kB

$ ssh prod-23-04 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
11726 MiB, 16384 MiB
```

mike: ok. looks like multiple nodes hitting high resident mem due to kv-cache not compacting. can we trigger immediate compaction and reduce kv TTL? any way to shed load?

ashley: yes. plan: 1) reduce kv cache TTL from 30m -> 2m for affected pool 2) run force compactor on nodes showing fragmentation 3) route traffic away using runtime routing policy (scale-down connections) until we see stable mem. running compaction now on prod-23-04: `./kv_compactor --pool prod-23 --force --dry-run=false`

devops-bot: Run initiated by ashley. Job #compaction-1749990000 started on prod-23-04.

support-lead: customer-impact: we're seeing ~120 requests/min with 500s in region us-west-2, roughly 0.8% of production traffic. Affected customers: heartbeat-tier customers (ids: C-1023, C-1108). Please prepare short customer note if we need extended mitigation.

mike: good call. start routing policy: move traffic off prod-23 into standby pool (policy: latency-first -> capacity fallback). Applying now.

infra-bot: routing update: prod-23 drained of new traffic, existing in-flight allowed to finish (graceful 30s).

ashley: compactor output: freed ~1.2GB resident on prod-23-04 after two passes. fragmentation metric down from 0.42 -> 0.15. monitoring.

ashley: follow-up logs:
```
[11:24:33] kv_compactor: pass1 freed 512MB
[11:25:10] kv_compactor: pass2 freed 704MB
[11:26:05] kv_cache: fragmentation=0.15, estimated-resident=10500MB
```

mike: good. OOM spike dropped to zero on that host. any alerts left?

incident-bot: alert status: degraded -> recovered for node prod-23-04. Still watching prod-23-02 (mem trend +12% over 30m).

carlos: I pulled heap profiles — leaking pattern points to page allocator not releasing free slots when eviction hits fragmentation threshold. Looks like allocator skip path (rare) where free segments are left in LRU but not returned to GPU memory. Possibly race during compaction + concurrent KV insert.

ashley: note: we hit a kernel launch error earlier which may be unrelated but indicates the runtime was under memory pressure when launching batched kernels. Until we patch, we should avoid long-lived sessions > 30m on heavy-kv flows.

mike: mitigation checklist (short):
- [x] drain prod-23 for new traffic
- [x] run forced compaction on affected nodes
- [x] reduce kv TTL for affected pool
- [x] monitor OOM alerts and CPU/gpu mem trends
- [ ] schedule rolling restart on nodes with fragmentation > 0.3
- [ ] issue customer-facing status if impact persists > 30m

support-lead: thanks. I'm drafting a status update for heartbeat-tier customers saying we've identified memory fragmentation causing instability, mitigations applied, monitoring closely. Will post in 10m unless conditions worsen.

devops-bot: compaction job #compaction-1749990000 completed on prod-23-04. exit=0

ashley: started compaction on prod-23-02 now; initial pass freed 400MB. will keep compactor running as background sweep.

carlos: proposed long-term fixes (post-incident):
- backport allocator patch that returns freed page segments immediately (PR #4521)
- add automatic compaction trigger when fragmentation > 0.35 or resident growth > 8% in 15m
- telemetry: add per-pool fragmentation histograms + compaction run traces
- runbook: how to safely drain and target compaction without customer-visible disruption

mike: agree. also add temporary rule for routing: if node mem > 85% route to fallback pool automatically.

infra-bot: prod-23-02 compaction freed 1.1GB after 3 passes; fragmentation now 0.18. no further OOMs on that node.

ashley: final notes: compaction reduced OOM rate but root cause is allocator race in paged-attention/KV allocation under long-running high-concurrency. we'll ship hotfix to runtime (small allocator guard) and schedule full allocator refactor.

mike: ok wrapping up oncall. handoff to next oncall @carlos at 12:00 UTC. CARLOS, please pick up postmortem and coordinate with infra + runtime teams.

carlos: will do. creating incident ticket INC-1749990000, assigning owners for backport + runbook + telemetry.

mike: thanks everyone. support-lead, please send the customer note when ready. I'll update PagerDuty and mark as monitored. :thumbsup:

support-lead: posting customer note now: "We've identified and mitigated a memory fragmentation issue affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. Mitigations applied; services stable. We'll follow up with a root cause analysis and timeline for the fix."

incident-bot: Incident INC-1749990000 status -> monitored. next update in 30m or on status change.
